TripDetective
ML Ratchet · vehicles · Phase 2

TripDetective

Give it one trip log, the kind a cheap OBD logger writes: speed, fuel rate, engine rpm, maybe battery current. It works out what kind of car drove it, how heavy it is, how big the engine is, how slippery it is, and where the energy went. Every answer comes with an error bar, and more trips of the same car make the answer tighter.

Trained only on simulated cars (RoadSim) driven over real Ann Arbor roads and logged by an emulated OBD logger. Graded on 351 real cars from the Vehicle Energy Dataset that were never used to choose anything.

Lab · simulated cars you can change

Change the car. Does the Detective notice?

Three simulated cars, each driven over the same two real Ann Arbor routes. Add mass, make it less slippery, swap its control strategy. The logs were precomputed with RoadSim and the OBD emulator; the network reads them live.

What this lab shows: the Detective follows mass only weakly (about a quarter of a change shows up) and hardly follows CdA at all. On real cars it gets mass right mostly from what kind of car it is (engine, fuel use, hybrid behaviour), not from reading the physics of each acceleration. See Limits.

Energy ledger · simulated twins only

Where the energy went

No real car comes with a measured energy ledger, so the ledger is graded only on simulated twins: each dev car's real trips re-driven by its RoadSim twin and logged with its own channels. The numbers below are simulator truth, not real truth.

The ratchet

Every rung, kept or not

A rung is kept only if it beats the incumbent's skill on a frozen simulated set by more than 0.01 and does not get worse on the 16 real dev cars (mean of mass and displacement errors no more than 5 % worse; VED-type accuracy no more than 0.03 lower).

How it was built

Physics first, graded on reality

1 · roadsReal routes1,154 Ann Arbor trip fragments from 17 unlabelled VED cars (lidar grade, airport weather), 10 test cycles, synthetic stop-and-go.
2 · carsRoadSimRandom light-duty cars of 7 layouts and 14 control strategies, driven second by second; every joule booked in a ledger.
3 · loggerOBD emulatorSignals polled on their own clocks (speed 1 s, MAF and rpm 2 s, load 5 s), held, quantised, MAF-estimated fuel, dropouts, random channel sets.
4 · twinsDev calibrationThe 16 dev cars' real trips re-driven by their twins; mismatches fixed in wrappers (engine efficiency, idle, hybrid thresholds, HVAC, fleet mass).
5 · networkCNN + poolingA 1-D CNN per trip plus 16 classical numbers (a least-squares road-load fit, idle fuel, rpm per speed); trips of one car averaged.

Physics

RoadSim (Phase 1) is forward-facing at 1 Hz: aero drag with the wind along the heading, rolling resistance with temperature and tyre warm-up, grade, inertia; EPA ALPHA engine and motor maps; automatic, CVT, DCT and power-split transmissions; a Thevenin battery; HVAC. Its checks: road-load force within 1.6 % of 47 real EPA coast-down targets; FTP +5.6 %, highway −4.3 % against EPA tests; energy ledger closes to 5e-4 on 600 stress runs.

What the network sees

Per second: speed, acceleration, grade, temperature, headwind, air density, fuel rate, rpm, battery power, SOC, A/C power, a validity mask and which channels exist, plus three road-load power channels. Per trip: the classical estimates. Trips over 17 minutes are cut into windows and pooled like separate trips. 0.4 M parameters.

Calibration on dev only

The twin test found older engines burn about 12 % more than the modern maps, idle faster, and that real hybrids (mostly older Priuses in Michigan) run the engine about twice as often while moving. The biggest single win came from the fleet: the generator's modern cars have a median mass of 2,200 kg; the dev and unlabelled VED cars, 1,720 kg. Matching that prior cut the dev mass bias from +106 kg to −9 kg.

Error bars

Every number is a mean and a log-sigma trained with a Gaussian likelihood. Sigmas are then widened, never narrowed, by one factor per output fitted on the dev cars: mass ×1.0, engine ×2.0 per car (×1.4 per trip).

Limits

Where it fails

  • It reads the kind of car more than the physics of each push. In the lab, adding 800 kg moves its mass estimate by only about 200 kg, and a 75 % change in CdA barely registers. With 1 Hz OBD signals (MAF fuel lags and holds for 2 s), efficiency, mass and drag trade off against each other, so the network leans on fleet regularities. Pooling 32 trips only cuts the real mass error from 153 to 126 kg.
  • Engines read small. Median engine error 0.50 L (22 %), biased −0.48 L: big V6/V8s are pulled toward the light-car prior. It beats a dev-median guess (25 %) only narrowly. Every rung that used the dev-calibrated priors made dev engines worse, which is why the ratchet rejected four of them.
  • The rule baseline wins on architecture. "Engine off while moving → hybrid; battery logged → plug-in" gets 99.4 % of cars, the Detective 98.9 % (four hybrids called conventional). In VED the battery channel exists only on plug-ins, which makes the task easy for any method.
  • The two exam Leafs read 460 kg too heavy. The simulator's 2013 Leaf uses about 1.5 × the battery energy of the real one (twin test; cabin heating too strong), so a real Leaf looks like a heavier car. Only 3 Leafs exist in VED.
  • Road-load force is about 15 % high at low speed on the 25 graded cars, mostly plug-ins. CdA and Crr are weakly identified in simulation too (skill 0.06 and 0.15).
  • The energy ledger has no real truth. On twins it beats a median guess for aero, rolling, braking, powertrain losses and auxiliaries, but not for net grade work.
  • Light duty only. No buses or trucks in training; ZTBus is not graded.
  • Simulator limits carry over: P2 hybrids optimistic in town, cold weather too mild, conventional A/C too cheap (RoadSim LIMITS.md).
Release

Use it

numpy + scipy only. Unzip tripdetective-v1.0.zip, then:

import tripdetective as TD
td = TD.TripDetective()
car = td.read_car([trip1, trip2])        # dicts of 1 Hz arrays: v, grade, T_amb, wind..., fuel_rate, engine_rpm, batt_current...
car['type_probs']                         # {'ICE': 0.98, 'HEV': 0.01, ...}
car['curb_kg'], car['mass_kg_1sigma']     # mass with its error bar
car['displacement_L'], car['CdA_m2'], car['Crr'], car['strategy']
car['ledger_kJ_per_km'][0]                # aero, rolling, grade, brake, powertrain, aux for trip 1

$ python3 demo.py                         # four real VED exam cars, a few seconds

  • US EPA test-car lists 2008-2026, dynamometer drive schedules and ALPHA engine/e-machine maps; fueleconomy.gov vehicles.csv. Public domain.
